questions.stem: Which expression gives the length of an arc that subtends an angle $\theta$ at the centre of a circle of radius $r$?
questions.explanation: An arc is part of the circumference, so take the fraction $\frac{\theta}{360}$ of $2\pi r$. Because $\theta$ is at most 360, this fraction is at most 1, so the arc can never exceed the full circumference.

distractorRationale.b: This is the sector area, since it uses $\pi r^2$
distractorRationale.c: The fraction is inverted, which would make small angles give huge arcs
distractorRationale.d: Missing the division by 360, so the units of angle are never converted to a fraction

questions.stem: Find the length of an arc of a circle of radius 7 cm which subtends an angle of $90°$ at the centre. Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
questions.explanation: The full circumference is $2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 44$ cm. A $90°$ angle is a quarter of the circle, so the arc is $\frac{1}{4} \times 44 = 11$ cm.

distractorRationale.b: Took half the circumference instead of a quarter
distractorRationale.c: This is the sector area in cm², not the arc length
distractorRationale.d: Gave the whole circumference

questions.stem: Find the area of a sector of a circle of radius 7 cm with an angle of $90°$ at the centre. Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
questions.explanation: The area of the whole circle is $\frac{22}{7} \times 49 = 154$ cm². A $90°$ sector is a quarter of it, so the area is $\frac{154}{4} = 38.5$ cm².

distractorRationale.a: This is the arc length in cm, a length rather than an area
distractorRationale.c: Took half the circle rather than a quarter
distractorRationale.d: Gave the area of the whole circle

questions.stem: An arc subtends an angle of $60°$ at the centre of a circle of radius 21 cm. Find the length of the arc, taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
questions.explanation: The circumference is $2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 = 132$ cm. Since $\frac{60}{360} = \frac{1}{6}$, the arc is $\frac{132}{6} = 22$ cm.

distractorRationale.a: Divided by 12 instead of 6
distractorRationale.c: Took half the circumference
distractorRationale.d: Gave the whole circumference

questions.stem: Find the perimeter, in centimetres, of a sector of radius 14 cm with an angle of $90°$ at the centre. Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: The circumference is $2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 = 88$ cm, so the arc is $\frac{88}{4} = 22$ cm. The perimeter also includes both radii, so it is $22 + 14 + 14 = 50$ cm. Leaving out the radii is the usual mistake here.

questions.stem: An arc of length 11 cm subtends an angle of $90°$ at the centre of a circle. Find the radius of the circle, taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
questions.explanation: Since the arc is a quarter of the circumference, the whole circumference is $4 \times 11 = 44$ cm. Then $2\pi r = 44$, so $r = \frac{44 \times 7}{2 \times 22} = 7$ cm.

distractorRationale.c: Used the diameter instead of the radius
distractorRationale.d: Gave the circumference rather than the radius

questions.stem: A sector of angle $216°$ is cut from a circle of radius 5 cm and folded to form a cone. Find the base radius of the cone.
questions.explanation: When the sector is folded, its arc becomes the circumference of the cone's base. The arc is $\frac{216}{360} \times 2\pi(5) = 0.6 \times 10\pi = 6\pi$. Setting $2\pi r = 6\pi$ gives $r = 3$ cm.
